person_note: The quote set repeatedly exposes Joe Coutts as a participating first-person narrator, including explicit retrospective contrasts between his younger and adult selves. Authorized opening prose independently confirms sustained first-person narration, while university and scholarly whole-book sources identify adult Joe as the controlling retrospective narrator and distinguish other characters' stories as embedded voices. Linda's first-person account and Bazil's legal explanation are therefore local material, not changes to a different grammatical-person base; in any event, Linda also speaks in first person. No credible source indicates sustained second- or third-person base sections. The only remaining uncertainty concerns attribution of a few clipped or boundary-stripped individual quotes, which does not affect the high-confidence FIRST classification.
